insights.text: Dario Amodei published 'We Must Pace the Frontier,' a three-step plan (embedded third-party evaluators with employee-level access, democratic-lab coordination on safety standards, global coordination with authoritarian states) arguing AI capability is outrunning alignment and interpretability work. Sam Altman endorsed it within hours ('I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier') and committed OpenAI to the same evaluator-access step; Elon Musk posted 'Dario is right.' The essay lands three days after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned publicly warning both Anthropic and OpenAI are 'racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.'

asgeirtj/system_prompts_leaks (GitHub #3, +217 stars/day, 65,535 total) now headlines extracted system prompts for Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5, and Claude Design -- the same repo that headlined Claude Fable 5's leaked prompt within days of its July release, confirming vendor system prompts now commoditize on a predictable, sub-week cadence.

Two independently-branded offensive-security agent tools trended the same day: SnailSploit/Claude-Red (a curated offensive-security skill library) and vxcontrol/pentagi ('fully autonomous AI Agents system capable of performing complex penetration testing'), extending the security-research-vertical skill genre this vault first tracked in August via zhaoxuya520/reverse-skill.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash holds Hugging Face Trending #1 (2,033 likes/140,636 downloads, up from yesterday's 1,870/75,774) on its claimed novel encoder-decoder architecture; Qwen3.8-27B's unsloth GGUF quantization now shows more downloads (11.5M) than the base model itself.

Yesterday's three-way convergence of independently-branded 'agent research to wiki' repos (hyperresearch, OpenResearch, llm_wiki) -- all shipping the same scrape-then-research-agent-then-wiki-compile architecture this vault's own daily pipeline runs -- doesn't recur on today's GitHub Trending board, one day into the two-week window set to test whether it was a genuine category or launch-day coincidence.
